texts.orig: Proof. Suppose we are given any target pivotals F W,r = { ( ℓ 1 i , ℓ 2 i , y i ) } i =1 ,...,M ∗ with M ∗ ≤ M 0 . If we perform the resampling operation, then with uniformly positive probability (depending on M 0 , r ) we sample ˜ M = M ∗ and the points w i ∈ D W,r/ 2 such that w i ∈ B ( y i , r/ 2) for every i = 1 , . . . , M ∗ . In particular, the strands ℓ 1 i , ℓ 2 i cross the annulus A ( w i , r, 2 r ). On the event E δ the strands of Γ ∗ ,B ( w i , 2 r ) ,B ( w i ,r ) out are δ -separated. Therefore, by Corollary 3.16, the probability that ℓ 1 i , ℓ 2 i switch their linking pattern after performing the resampling is bounded from below uniformly in δ . Moreover, by continuity (Theorem 1.7) we see that with positive probability bounded from below the new strands ℓ res , 1 i , ℓ res , 2 i intersect again inside B ( w i , r/ 2). (Although we have not phrased the topology (1.2) to keep track of the intersection points between the chords, the proof of Theorem 1.7 shows that continuity also holds when we require the intersection sets to converge.) Repeating this argument M ∗ times for each target pivotal, we conclude. □
